title: Heterogeneous circuit safeguards and progressive detour routing for dependency/model outages
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement a heterogeneous circuit breaker framework that operates at dependency, model-variant, and tenant granularity and enables progressive detour routing (warm-standby models, cached responses, degraded feature paths) with clearly defined trip thresholds and safe rollback. This ticket defines the design, threshold heuristics, fallback modes, observability changes, and rollout plan. The objective is to reduce P95 latency and error exposure during partial outages while preserving availability for critical customers and minimizing data-safety risk for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: CB framework can be configured per dependency, per model variant, and per tenant via config API
Three fallback modes implemented: (1) local cache/short-circuit, (2) warm-standby model routing, (3) degraded-response with partial outputs and explanation metadata
Thresholds configurable by policy and by cohort; default policy trips at documented SLO-derived values
Observability: per-breaker metric (state, trip reason, duration), event feed to console, and SLO dashboard showing impact on error budget
Automated canary rollout: new breaker logic enabled in a limited cohort and validated by synthetic traffic before global rollout
Playbook: on-trip runbook with automated and manual responder actions and safe-rollback path
metrics: Primary trip signals: 5xx rate (>1.0% over 120s) | p95 latency (>3000ms over 60s) | queue length (>75 over 30s)
Secondary signals: K/V cache miss rate (>30% for 3m), GPU-sched queue growth (sustained >90% utilization for 2m)
Grace thresholds: Tiered buckets (warning, soft-trip, hard-trip) where soft-trip triggers reduced-quality fallback and hard-trip triggers full detour routing
SLO correlation: link trip events to per-tenant 99/95 latency and error budget burn; provide delta view in the Console
implementation_notes: Design a small extensible state machine for breakers: CLOSED -> WARN -> SOFT_TRIPPED -> HARD_TRIPPED -> RECOVERING. State transitions driven by sliding-window EWMA and absolute counters.
Per-tenant policy overrides: default policy in config service; tenant-specific overrides stored encrypted for Private customers and respected by coordinator at request time
Fallback routing decisions must be idempotent and attach deterministic metadata to responses (fallback_reason, fallback_path, original_model_id)
Safe-fallback rules: do not fallback to a model variant that violates customer pinned versions or to a model that has telemetry-disabled for Private deployments
Rate-limited degraded responses: when in SOFT_TRIPPED state, prefer returning cached/partial results up to X rps per-tenant and mark response with 'partial:true' and 'explanation' field
Ensure KV cache cold-start behavior: do not use cached responses older than TTL or with stale-signature for PHI-sensitive tenant labels
Integration points: router service, model catalog (for warm-standby candidates), cache service, console event stream, and runbook automation hooks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit + integration tests; feature flags behind 'hetero-cb' gate; no runtime behavior change
Phase 1: Enable for internal traffic only (redwood-infra, dev teams) and run synthetic SLO tests for 48h
Phase 2: Canary -> 2% of production traffic (region us-west-2) for 24h, monitor trip rate and customer-impact delta
Phase 3: Gradual expansion by region and tenant cohort with automated rollback if error budget burn increases >5% relative to baseline
Phase 4: Full rollout, then tighten default thresholds and publish runbook/console docs
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We choose tiered soft/hard trips instead of single binary breakers to preserve availability and offer controlled quality degradation (tradeoff: more complex state machine & testing)
Fallback to smaller or quantized model variants prioritized over cross-region failover to avoid data egress for Private deployments (tradeoff: potential quality regression)
Default thresholds are conservative (favor availability) but tenants can opt into aggressive thresholds for cost-savings
Keeping per-tenant overrides increases config complexity and operational surface; mitigated by exposing a validation API and automated linting of policies
qa_plan: Unit tests for state transitions including flapping protection and hysteresis
Integration tests that simulate dependency slowdowns and confirm fallback path selection
Chaos tests: inject 5xx spikes, latency increases, and cache failures across regions to validate multi-region detour and rollback
Load tests exercising queue growth scenarios to validate queue-length-based tripping
Security review focusing on Private tenant constraints: ensure no cached PHI leakage during fallback
